output.methodChoice: Collected X14 (per-cell timing of gateway and config changes) and X7 (storage-node disk and compaction metrics). Compared each rival explanation against the per-cell timelines, the one cell that skipped the config push, the 6 Nov gateway rollback test, and the on-node timing data.
output.brief:
Priya, gateway 5.8 is not behind the latency jump. The cause is the storage team's compaction tuning change (FC-7710), pushed fleet-wide on the evening of 2 Nov. It tripled compaction workers (2 to 6), drove disks from 41% to 97% busy, and reads now wait about 200 ms in disk queues, matching the p99 jump.

Evidence: in every cell the slowdown started within minutes of that push, whatever gateway version it ran; eu-w cells slowed 2.5–4 hours before 5.8 reached them. One cell, aps-3, runs 5.8 but skipped the push and stayed near 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 on 6 Nov changed nothing. The network fault began after the slowdown, and fixing it changed nothing. GET traffic grew only about 6%, aps-3 included.

Next: don't roll back the gateway; it won't help and reopens the signature flaw before the 30 Nov audit deadline. Revert FC-7710 in one cell, watch p99 and backlog, then extend. Don't pause compaction. Hold any Orrin rate limit until the backlog attribution on 10 Nov; backlog is 4%, not projected to reach 15% before 13 Nov. Record config pushes on the shared calendar.

Confidence: about 90% on cause; backlog source unknown.
